core_obligations: First implication (proof lines 12445-12450): if E is represented by a complex of flat modules vanishing outside [a, b], the derived tensor product with any module is the ordinary tensor product, so the Tor groups vanish outside the interval.

Reduce to bounded above (proof lines 12452-12467): represent E by a bounded above complex of flat modules K^bullet and let n be the largest index with K^n nonzero; if n > b then H^n(K^bullet) = 0 makes K^{n-1} -> K^n surjective, so the kernel is flat and one may replace K^bullet by its truncation tau_{<= n-1}; induction on n reduces to the case where K^i = 0 for i > b.

Truncate from below (proof lines 12468-12469): setting E^bullet = tau_{>= a}K^bullet, everything is clear except flatness of E^a, which follows from the last-one-flat criterion applied to K^{a-1} -> K^a and the definitions.
proof_roadmap: Read the first implication off the flat representative.
Truncate the bounded above flat representative above b by induction, using flatness of kernels of surjections of flat modules.
Truncate below a and use the last-one-flat criterion for flatness of the new degree-a term.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises tor amplitude in a bounded interval through representability by a bounded complex of flat modules on a ringed site (statement lines 12431-12442). The proof (proof lines 12444-12469) reads one implication off the flat representative, reduces the other to a bounded above flat representative by induction using flatness of kernels of surjections of flat modules, and finishes by truncating below and applying the last-one-flat criterion. H2: two truncation steps with a flatness input, written out.
